newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech May M2 money supply +6.8 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Czech May M2 money supply +6.8 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The Czech National Bank's (CNB) key money supply measure, M2, grew 6.8 percent year-on-year in May, excluding the influence of funds from the selloff in 1995 of a stake in telephone operator SPT Telecom, the CNB said.
The statement added that including SPT funds, year-on-year money supply growth for May was 6.1 percent.
In April, M2 grew 6.2 percent, year-on-year, without the influence of SPT funds, and 5.3 percent including the $1.32 billion from the 1995 equity expansion and sale of a stake in SPT.

The statement said the total volume of crown and foreign currency credits in May rose 13.3 percent year-on-year, after 11.6 percent growth in April, while total crown and foreign currency deposits, which include the SPT funds, grew 5.7 percent after a 4.6 percent rise in April.
The statement said the average interest rate for new crown credits in May was 21.56 percent, some 813 basis points higher than in April.
CZECH M2 MONEY MAY 1997 APRIL 1997 MAY 1996
*Includes domestic deposits connected to the $1.32 billion equity expansion of SPT Telecom a.s. in summer 1995.
The average interest rate for new credits comes after a crown crisis in May forced the central bank to raise interest rates sharply and choke market liquidity.
